tags.description: Identify the product’s visible front or principal face, including its actual packaging front; do not guess orientation from an ambiguous crop.
Identify a visible brand mark on the actual product or packaging; exclude watermarks, promotional overlays and branding on unrelated props.
Identify visible human contact with the actual product, such as holding, touching or carrying; a nearby person alone is insufficient.
Identify the product or attributable application/result in a relevant setting with visible contextual detail; a plain backdrop alone does not qualify.
Identify a visibly supported side/profile surface; a three-quarter image may also show a front or back surface.
Identify a recognizable close-up of product texture, finish, colour, joins or construction; do not infer material composition.
Identify actual visible bowl, vessel, chamber, tray or cooking-contact surfaces of this item.
Identify the item visibly arranged for its documented preparation, cooking or serving role; props need not be included and a still does not prove operation.
Identify actual visible cavity trays, supports and vessel interior; do not invent concealed stacked trays.
Identify the actual vessel with an evident open or removed lid where supplied; a tray-only image does not establish lid position.
Identify separate products of the same kind shown as a catalog assortment, including variants; exclude repeated views of one item, unrelated props and packaging art mistaken for units.
Identify different product types visibly represented together as a catalog set, supported by item context; exclude unrelated props, duplicate views and packaging art mistaken for actual items.

Ignore only when neither the catalog product nor an attributable application/result or contents depiction is identifiable, or dominant text prevents assessing that evidence. Unbranded items are valid.
